meta.name: Cockapoo
meta.tagline: The Cockapoo, a Cocker Spaniel crossed with a Poodle, is a friendly, trainable Doodle that comes in toy, mini and standard sizes. Its biggest health watch-outs are ear infections and itchy skin, and no US Cockapoo registry checks breeders' health tests, so verifying the two purebred parents is up to you.
meta.excerpt: Cockapoos are friendly, trainable Cocker Spaniel–Poodle crosses that come in three sizes. Ear infections and itchy skin are the main health watch-outs, and no US Cockapoo registry checks health tests, so verify the parents yourself.
meta.meta_description: Cockapoo guide: American vs English Cocker parents, toy to standard sizes, ear infection risk, the health tests to ask for, grooming, and cost ranges.
meta.quick_answer: The Cockapoo is a small-medium designer crossbreed, weighing Toy under 12 · Mini 13–20 · Std 21+ lbs and living 12–15 years. Plan on 30–60 min of exercise a day. Grooming is high (pro every 4–8 wks); training is easy. It is good with kids. It is a realistic choice for a first-time owner.

intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: What Is a Cockapoo?
intro.html:
The Cockapoo is a cross between a Cocker Spaniel and a Poodle, usually a Miniature or Toy Poodle. It's one of the oldest designer crosses: the Cockapoo Club of GB says the dogs have been known in the United States since about 1950, with the earliest dictionary mention in a 1960 Oxford English Dictionary citation. The appeal is simple: a cheerful, people-focused dog in a manageable size, with a Poodle-influenced coat.

Cockapoos aren't an AKC breed, and the US club picture is messy. The Cockapoo Club of America's old web domain is now for sale. The American Cockapoo Club publishes a breed standard and runs a registry, but joining costs a one-time $50, and neither its membership terms nor its code of ethics requires a health test. Cockapoos can't get full AKC registration, though they can enroll in the AKC's Canine Partners program for mixed breeds.

The upshot: nobody in the US checks a Cockapoo breeder's health testing for you. This guide covers what to check instead, starting with which kind of Cocker is in the pedigree.

appearance.label: Physical
appearance.heading: What does a Cockapoo look like?
appearance.html:
Three sizes, set mostly by the Poodle parent

The American Cockapoo Club's standard sorts Cockapoos by height: 10 inches or under at the shoulder is a toy (ideally under 12 lbs), 11–14 inches is a mini (13–20 lbs), and 15 inches or more is a standard (21 lbs and up). The Poodle parent drives much of that. The AKC's Toy Poodle is 10 inches or under at 4–6 lbs, and the Miniature Poodle is 10–15 inches at 10–15 lbs. Littermates can still finish at different sizes, so ask for both parents' adult heights and weights.

American or English Cocker? It matters

Two Cocker breeds go into Cockapoos. The AKC's Cocker Spaniel (the American Cocker) is 13.5–15.5 inches and 20–30 lbs; the English Cocker Spaniel is 15–17 inches and 26–34 lbs. The Cockapoo Club of GB goes further, splitting the Cocker side into American show, English show and English working types that it says could be viewed as different breeds. We found no data on which type is most common in US Cockapoos, so ask the breeder. The answer changes which DNA tests to request (see Health).

Coat and color

The American Cockapoo Club describes tight-curl, medium-curl and flat coats, and says all three commonly appear in the same litter. That's genetics: three genes explain most coat differences in purebred dogs, covering curl, length and the Poodle's beard-and-eyebrow “furnishings” (Cadieu et al., 2009), and a first-cross (F1) puppy can inherit any mix. F1B Cockapoos (an F1 bred back to a Poodle) carry more Poodle ancestry, which makes a curly coat more likely but never guaranteed; multigeneration litters vary with how many Poodle back-crosses are in the pedigree. Colors span both parents, from black and chocolate to cream, apricot, red and parti-color.

temperament.label: Personality
temperament.heading: What is the temperament of a Cockapoo?
temperament.html:
The American Cockapoo Club's standard describes a people-oriented, outgoing, happy dog with a keen intelligence and a forgiving nature. That's a club describing its ideal, not a study, but it fits the parents: the AKC calls the Cocker Spaniel merry, responsive and energetic, and the Toy Poodle agile, self-confident and intelligent.

Next to a Cavapoo, the Cockapoo is the livelier of the two (see our Cavapoo vs Cockapoo comparison). Many enjoy fetch and long sniffing walks, a nod to the Cocker's sporting roots, and training is usually easy. They're friendly with visitors and generally sociable with other dogs, so don't expect a guard dog.

Two cautions. The same standard says Cockapoos are people dogs that shouldn't be left alone for extended periods, so a home that's empty from 9 to 5 needs a plan. And crosses vary: a 2022 study of 18,385 dogs found breed explained only about 9% of the behavioral differences between individual dogs (Morrill et al.). Meet the mother if you can and judge the individual puppy. With children, Cockapoos suit kids who are gentle and supervised; a 10-lb toy is far easier to injure than a 25-lb standard.

mikes_take.label: A Realistic Take
mikes_take.heading: What I'd Tell a Friend Thinking About a Cockapoo
mikes_take.html:
A well-bred Cockapoo can be a genuinely good family dog: friendly, trainable and a manageable size. If you want a cheerful dog that will walk, fetch and then nap on the sofa, it's a sensible pick. I'd go in with clear eyes on three things.

First, don't buy one for the allergy promise. In a Dutch study, so-called hypoallergenic breeds had higher levels of the main dog allergen in their coats than other dogs, with no difference in airborne allergen at home (Vredegoor et al., 2012), and a US study of household dust found no difference either (Nicholas et al., 2011). If someone at home is allergic, spend real time with the specific dog first. Our hypoallergenic breeds guide explains what low-shedding can and can't do.

Second, don't count on hybrid vigor. In a 2024 UK survey covering 1,856 Cockapoos, they matched Cocker Spaniels on 49 of 57 disorders and had higher odds of ear infections and itchy skin (Bryson et al.). Choose a Cockapoo because you like the dog, then budget for ear and skin care.

Third, the paperwork is your job. “ACC registered” means the breeder paid the club's $50 joining fee and registered the litter, not that the parents were tested. Get the parents' registered names and look them up on OFA. And price a groomer before you price a puppy: in a US survey, more than twice as many doodle owners as other owners said upkeep such as grooming was more work than they'd expected (Hladky-Krage & Hoffman, 2022).

care.label: Daily Life
care.heading: How much exercise and grooming does a Cockapoo need?
care.html:
Exercise

Plan on 30–60 minutes a day of walks and play. The AKC says the Cocker isn't a breed that needs a lot of exercise, while Poodles of every size need good exercise daily. A standard from English working Cocker lines may want more than an hour; a toy from show lines may be content with less.

Mental Stimulation

Short training sessions, food puzzles and scent games keep the Poodle brain busy. The AKC's Canine Partners program also opens agility, rally, scent work and Fast CAT to spayed or neutered mixed breeds.

Grooming

  • Brushing: Several times a week, and daily for curly or long coats, combing down to the skin behind the ears and under the legs. The AKC warns that missed Cocker grooming sessions lead to tangles and mats.
  • Professional grooming: Every 4–6 weeks (PetMD); a short clip plus home brushing can stretch that toward 6–8.
  • Ears: Check weekly (PetMD) and dry them after baths and swims. Long, hairy ear flaps are the Cockapoo's weak spot.
  • Teeth: Brush daily, as PetMD recommends.

The ear and coat routines in our Cocker Spaniel grooming guide apply to Cockapoos too.

Training

Usually easy with reward-based methods. Start puppy classes early, build alone time gradually from the first weeks, and expect housetraining a toy-size puppy to take extra patience.

health.label: Wellness
health.heading: What health problems are common in the Cockapoo?
health.html:
Cockapoo-specific health data is thin, but one large study stands out. A 2024 UK owner survey compared 1,856 Cockapoos with 2,237 Cocker Spaniels and 927 Poodles, all aged up to five (Bryson et al.). Against Cockers, Cockapoos showed no difference for 49 of 57 disorders, with higher odds of itching (2.67 times), ear infections (2.13 times) and vomiting, and lower odds of lameness, eye disorders, wounds and lumps. Against Poodles, there was no difference for 45 of 57, with lower odds of eye disorders, patellar luxation, food hypersensitivity, weight loss and dental disease, and higher odds of swallowed foreign bodies, anal sac problems, diarrhea and itching.

The data are owner-reported and from the UK, where English Cockers are the usual Cocker parent, so US dogs from American Cocker lines may differ. Lifespan is usually estimated at 12–15 years (PetMD); we found no Cockapoo longevity study.

ConditionWhat It Means
Ear Infections (Otitis Externa)The standout Cockapoo problem: about twice the Cocker's odds in the 2024 UK survey (odds ratio 2.13). In UK veterinary records, Cockapoos had 2.22 times the odds of ear infections of crossbred dogs, and floppy-eared dogs had 1.76 times the odds of upright-eared dogs (O'Neill et al., 2021). No screening test exists. Check and dry ears weekly, and see your vet at the first head-shaking, odor or redness.
Itchy Skin (Pruritus)Higher odds than both parent breeds: 2.67 times the Cocker's and 1.5 times the Poodle's. Causes range from fleas to food and environmental allergies, so itching needs a vet workup. No breeder test exists.
Progressive Retinal Atrophy (prcd-PRA)Inherited blindness found in both parent breeds. The Poodle and English Cocker clubs require the DNA test, and the Cockapoo Club of GB makes a clear result its minimum for approved breeders. It's recessive: if one parent tests clear, no puppy can be affected.
Cataracts & Other Eye DiseaseThe AKC recommends an ophthalmologist exam for Cockers, and the Poodle club asks for one yearly on breeding Toy and Miniature Poodles. Ask for a current exam (often recorded as CAER) on both parents.
Hip DysplasiaHip evaluations are listed for Cockers (AKC and the English Cocker club) and Miniature Poodles (Poodle club). Ask for OFA or PennHIP results; final OFA hip ratings need the dog to be 24 months or older.
Patellar LuxationA slipping kneecap. The American College of Veterinary Surgeons says it's diagnosed in 7% of puppies and lists miniature poodles as predisposed. OFA patella exams are required for Toy and Miniature Poodles and English Cockers. Cockapoos had about half the Poodles' odds in the UK survey.
Familial Nephropathy (English Cocker lines)An inherited kidney disease with a DNA test. The Cockapoo Club of GB lists it for English show and working lines; the English Cocker club offers it as an elective test. It matters most for F2 and multigeneration litters, where both parents carry Cocker ancestry; the Cockapoo Club of GB makes the test mandatory for those later-generation litters.
PFK Deficiency (American Cocker lines)An inherited enzyme deficiency affecting red blood cells and muscles, with a DNA test. The Cockapoo Club of GB lists it for American Cocker lines. It matters most for F2 and multigeneration litters, where both parents carry Cocker ancestry; the Cockapoo Club of GB makes the test mandatory for those later-generation litters.
Dental DiseaseIn UK veterinary records, Cockapoos had 2.11 times the odds of gum (periodontal) disease of crossbred dogs after accounting for age and other factors, and the odds rose as bodyweight fell (O'Neill et al., 2021). No breeder test exists; brush daily.

Ask breeders for (by parent): Cocker parent: OFA or PennHIP hips, a current ophthalmologist eye exam and a prcd-PRA DNA result, plus PFK DNA for an American Cocker, or OFA patellas and familial nephropathy DNA for an English Cocker. Poodle parent: prcd-PRA DNA, an eye exam within the last year and OFA patellas, plus hips for a Miniature Poodle. Cockapoos have no OFA testing list of their own, so look up both parents' results by registered name at ofa.org.

cost.label: Budget
cost.heading: How much does a Cockapoo cost?
cost.html:
No reliable US survey tracks Cockapoo prices, so the puppy line is Wooffy's estimate, the same range as our Cavapoo vs Cockapoo comparison. Everything below is an estimated range. Most lines are Rover's 2026 figures for all breeds and sizes; Rover says small adult dogs can cost up to 63% less a year than large and giant breeds, so expect the lower part of the food, supplies and insurance ranges. Rover's annual table has no professional-grooming line, so we added it at Thumbtack's national averages ($79–$136 a session) every 4–8 weeks.

Add grooming to Rover's totals, and swap the adoption fee for the puppy price if you buy. The North American Pet Health Insurance Association reports the average US accident-and-illness premium for a dog was $836 in 2025. Under the NAIC's model pet insurance law, which states adopt individually, insurers must disclose hereditary, congenital and pre-existing-condition exclusions, so read them before enrolling, ideally before any ear or skin problem is on record. Rover also suggests setting aside $300–$2,500 for emergency vet bills.

right_for_you.label: Fit Assessment
right_for_you.heading: Is a Cockapoo Right for You?
good_fit: Families who want a cheerful, trainable small-to-medium dog that enjoys walks and play
Someone home much of the day, or a dog walker or daycare plan (the breed club says they shouldn't be left alone for long stretches)
Owners ready for brushing several times a week, weekly ear checks and a groomer every 4–8 weeks
First-time owners willing to do puppy classes and reward-based training
Buyers who will check the purebred parents' health results on OFA themselves
not_fit: Allergy sufferers counting on a “hypoallergenic” label; the research doesn't support it
Households where the dog would be alone 8+ hours most days
Owners who want a wash-and-go coat; mats form fast when brushing slips
Anyone not prepared for recurring ear and skin vet visits
Buyers who need a predictable adult size and coat; even littermates vary

finding.label: Next Steps
finding.heading: Where can you find a Cockapoo puppy or rescue?
finding.html:
Buying from a Breeder

No US Cockapoo club verifies health testing: the American Cockapoo Club's breeder list is a paid listing with no testing rule, and the Cockapoo Club of America no longer has a working website. So you're vetting two purebred parents. Ask which Cocker type and Poodle size they are, get their registered names, and check the OFA database. Our guide on how to find a responsible breeder shows how to read the results, and our Doodle breeding ethics guide covers the wider doodle market.

For benchmarks, the American Spaniel Club, the English Cocker Spaniel Club of America and the Poodle Club of America publish breeder lists and testing expectations for the purebred parents. In the UK, the Cockapoo Club of GB's approved breeders are inspected and need at least a clear prcd-PRA result.

Walk away from “vet-checked” in place of OFA results, parents with no registered names, a promised hypoallergenic puppy, or an offer to ship a puppy you haven't seen with its mother. In a UK study, only 41% of designer-cross buyers asked for and saw the parents' health-screening results, versus 54% of purebred buyers (Burnett et al., 2022). Our puppy scams guide covers the payment and shipping tricks.

Rescue

Search Petfinder and Adopt a Pet by breed and set alerts. IDOG Rescue, a national foster-based doodle rescue (fees $100–$1,000, depending on the dog), and the Poodle Club of America Rescue Foundation, which points adopters to regional Poodle rescues, are worth asking about Cockapoos. UK readers can try Cockapoo Rescue GB. An adult comes with a known size, coat and temperament. Torn? Read our adopt or shop guide.

faq.a: No dog is, and the research doesn't back the label. Studies found so-called hypoallergenic breeds had more of the main dog allergen in their coats than other dogs, no less airborne allergen in their homes, and no difference in household dust. Curly Cockapoos often shed less visible hair, but coats vary even within a litter. If someone at home has dog allergies, spend time with the specific dog first and talk to an allergist.

It depends on the Poodle parent's size and the Cocker type. The American Cockapoo Club sorts adults by height: toys are 10 inches or under (ideally under 12 lbs), minis 11–14 inches (about 13–20 lbs) and standards 15 inches and up (21 lbs and up). Both parents' adult sizes are a better guide than any puppy estimate.

About 12–15 years is the usual estimate (PetMD). We found no Cockapoo-specific longevity study, so be skeptical of claims of 16–20 years. For reference, the AKC gives 10–14 years for the Cocker Spaniel, 12–14 for the English Cocker and 10–18 for Toy and Miniature Poodles.

They can. There's no data on how often, but the American Cockapoo Club's own standard says Cockapoos are people dogs that shouldn't be left alone for extended periods, and PetMD notes they can be a bit anxious and develop separation anxiety. Teach alone time gradually from puppyhood, and plan for a dog walker or daycare if everyone works long days away.

faq.q: What's the difference between an F1 and an F1B Cockapoo?
faq.a: An F1 is a purebred Cocker Spaniel bred to a purebred Poodle. An F1B is an F1 Cockapoo bred back to a Poodle, so it carries more Poodle ancestry and is more likely to have a curly coat that sheds less hair. F2 and multigeneration Cockapoos come from Cockapoo-to-Cockapoo breeding. No generation guarantees a coat type.

faq.q: What's the difference between American and English Cockapoos?
faq.a: The difference is the Cocker parent. The American Cocker (the AKC's Cocker Spaniel) is about 20–30 lbs with a heavy coat; the English Cocker Spaniel is taller and heavier at about 26–34 lbs. The type affects size and coat, and it changes the DNA tests to ask for: PFK deficiency for American Cocker lines and familial nephropathy for English lines, per the Cockapoo Club of GB.

faq.q: How much does a Cockapoo cost?
faq.a: No reliable US price survey exists. Wooffy's estimate for a breeder puppy is $1,500–$3,500, and Rover's 2026 data puts breeder prices across all dogs at $675–$4,440; shelter adoption fees run about $50–$500 (Rover), and some doodle rescues charge up to $1,000. Rover puts the yearly cost of an adult dog at $1,930–$5,305 before professional grooming, which adds roughly $515–$1,770. All are estimated ranges.
